raw_answer_text:
A1: In this genre the default is a total order, so the message drawn higher on that lifeline occurs strictly before the one drawn lower — the two event occurrences are ordered, not concurrent.
A2: Exactly one operand executes on any run, and the guard on each operand decides which one — "accepted" or "rejected."
A3: The file gives the loop's guard as "while no response, and fewer than 3 attempts made," so the operand may execute while that condition holds, up to at most 3 attempts; no explicit numeric lower bound is stated.
A4: The `par` fragment asserts that the profile-fetch and the audit-flush operands have no relative order to each other; it nevertheless still requires the order of the messages within each individual operand.
A5: It asserts the single operand's behaviour (the expanded-profile reply) either runs or does not run, with no alternative to choose between.
A6: The critical fragment contains the message "write: token issued" (s -> a).
A7: The second operand of the alt contains the message "401 Unauthorized" (c <- s), corresponding to the "rejected" guard.
A8: The remainder of the enclosing session is abandoned — the break operand runs instead of everything that would otherwise follow it.
